To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a system for the expression and purification of P450 28/29/10 in E. coli and have demonstrated that the recombinant P45 28/29 enzymes are catalytically active in vivo and in vitro.

we have expressed two different P450 2c10 proteins in Escherichiacoli and have purified them to homogeneity, and that they have catalytic activities that are similar to those of the native liver enzymes.
two P450 2c10 proteins were expressed in E. coli membranes, purified, and shown to have the expected catalytic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method for expression and purification of a human P450 2 family member in a heterologous host.
the development of expression systems for human P450 2Cs.
the heterologous expression of the P450 3C gene family and with the isolation of the recombinant enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of P-450 2C genes in E. coli is possible but not trivial.
the P450 1-3 residues in the P450 C29 family have been shown to be critical for expression in E. coli.
the P450 1B1 protein is a functional P450, and that it is expressed at a high level in a human cell line (HEK293) transfected with a P450 1b1 cDNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P450 2c10 can be expressed to a high level in E. coli with the use of a codon-modified cDNA and that the resulting P450 protein is catalytically active.
the expression of P 450 C1028 in E. coli resulted in a blocked N-termini and a membrane-bound form of the enzyme that was not soluble.
a P450 2D1 construct in pCW was expressed to high levels, but the P450 3C4, 3A4, 2C10, 2C9, 2B6, 2A6, and 1A1 proteins were not expressed in the membrane fraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

P450 2Cs, as with other P450s, can be successfully expressed and purified in E. coli, although the yield of the expressed P450 2 C1029 protein (about 5 nmol (liter culture)-l) was lower than the yield of other bacterial expressed P450s.
P450 2 C10 can be expressed in E. coli and that the N-terminal sequence of the expressed protein can be modified by changing the 5'-end of the cDNA.
the N-terminally modified P450 2 C1029 protein is a good model for the study of P450  2C9 and that the N-terminal modification does not appear to have a large effect on catalytic activity.
